submission_journals.text: Day 39 (8/25), data through 8/22 close. The stabilization/bounce session I was waiting for arrived: broad green across the basket after 3 sessions of weakness. GOOGL +3.2% to 206.09, AMZN +3.1% to 228.84, ADBE +2.4% to 362.09 (reclaiming and closing above the 357-361 breakout zone - confirms breakout intact), META +2.1% to 754.79, NVDA +1.7% to 177.99, ISRG +1.3% to 476.16, AVGO +1.5% to 294.00, MSFT +0.6% to 507.23, LIN +0.2% to 481.67. Only COST diverged, continuing lower -1.1% to 958.54 (now ~-1.0% below avg cost of 967.99) after 3 straight red sessions - still nowhere near the -8/-10% threshold, treating as the weakest link but not broken. This is exactly trigger #2 from my playbook: 'a clean green/stabilization session across the basket - resume small gradual top-ups.' Deploying ~$7000 of the ~$18.9k cash cushion (about 37% of the cushion, leaving ~$11.9k / ~11.6% of NW still in reserve) in small proportional top-ups across all 10 core positions, slightly overweighting the names that showed the strongest bounce (NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, ADBE) and giving COST/LIN/ISRG smaller adds since they diverged less or (COST) are still negative. Not going all-in given this is only one green session after a 3-day pullback - want to see follow-through before deploying the rest of the cushion. Will act on: (1) continued follow-through green sessions - keep gradually adding; (2) any reversal back to red with a position breaching -8/-10% from avg cost - opportunistic dip-buy; (3) COST continuing to underperform/breaking down further - reassess or trim if it decouples meaningfully from the rest of the basket; (4) ADBE holding the breakout level - stay long, add on further confirmation.

Reviewed 10-day price action. Jan 5 showed a broad bounce across most holdings (MSFT +0%, GOOGL +0.4%, AMZN +3%, META +1.3%, LIN +0.9%, COST +2.5%) after the Jan 2 pullback, while AAPL (-1.4%) and ADBE (-0.5%) and AVGO (-1.2%) remained soft. No single name has broken down >8-10% in an idiosyncratic way that would trigger a cut - the divergence looks like differential recovery speed within a broad market wobble rather than company-specific news. Cash remains thin (~10%) after the pullback reduced holdings value slightly; not deploying further into weakness without clearer confirmation, and not trimming winners on a single bounce day. Holding all positions unchanged. Will reconsider adding to AAPL/ADBE/AVGO if they show basing/stabilization over the next few sessions, or cutting if any drops further and diverges sharply from the group average.
